faqs.q: Is digital smile designing a treatment by itself?
faqs.a: No. Digital smile designing is a planning method in which the dentist uses photographs, videos and scans to design and preview your new smile. The actual change comes from treatments such as veneers, crowns, bonding, whitening, orthodontics or gum contouring, carried out according to that plan.

The design stage is not painful, because it involves only photographs, videos and scans of your teeth and face. Any discomfort depends on the treatment that follows, such as veneers or gum contouring, and your dentist will use local anaesthesia where it is needed.

faqs.q: Will my new smile look exactly like the digital preview?
faqs.a: The preview gives a close and realistic idea of the planned result, and you can ask for changes before treatment starts. Because it is a simulation, small differences are possible depending on your teeth, gums and the materials used, so discuss your expectations openly with your dentist.

faqs.q: Who can get digital smile designing?
faqs.a: Most adults planning a cosmetic change to their smile, such as veneers, crowns, gum contouring or straightening, can benefit from digital smile design planning. Your dentist will first check that your teeth and gums are healthy, because problems like decay or gum disease need treating before any cosmetic work.
